companies.name: Overland AI
companies.why: Off-road autonomy for military ground vehicles. Local and early, so equity still has room to grow.

companies.name: Anduril
companies.why: Autonomous defense hardware plus the software that ties it together. Has a Seattle office and an early-career track.

companies.name: Shield AI
companies.why: AI pilot software for drones and aircraft. Hires early-career engineers directly.

companies.name: Saronic
companies.why: Autonomous surface vessels for the Navy, scaling up its own shipbuilding.

companies.name: Helion
companies.why: Building a fusion power plant to sell electricity to Microsoft. A moonshot bet on cheap power for data centers.

companies.name: Zap Energy
companies.why: A smaller, simpler approach to fusion, built in the Seattle area.

companies.name: Crusoe
companies.why: Builds and runs AI data centers sited next to cheap energy.

companies.name: Baseten
companies.why: Runs other companies' AI models in production. Several roles list Seattle.

companies.name: Together AI
companies.why: GPU cloud and inference platform for open-source models.

companies.name: Modal
companies.why: Serverless GPUs, so developers run AI jobs without managing servers.

companies.name: Supabase
companies.why: Open-source Postgres backend that many new AI-built apps start on. Fully remote.

companies.name: Stripe
companies.why: Payments rails for the internet, now including AI companies. Large and stable but still private, with a real Seattle office.

companies.name: Figure
companies.why: Humanoid robots for factories and homes. A big, uncertain bet with huge upside if it works.

companies.name: Zipline
companies.why: Autonomous delivery drones already flying commercial routes. Real-world autonomy at scale.

companies.name: Relativity Space
companies.why: Building a reusable rocket to compete in the launch market. High risk, high upside.

companies.name: SpaceX
companies.why: Starlink is the cash machine: satellite internet sold to millions of homes, planes and ships, engineered in Redmond.

companies.name: Stoke Space
companies.why: Building a fully reusable rocket, plus Boltline, a software product other hardware companies pay for.

companies.name: Starfish Space
companies.why: Robot spacecraft that dock with satellites to refuel and extend them. Small team, early, local.

companies.name: Portal Space Systems
companies.why: Fast-moving spacecraft that can change orbits quickly, aimed at defense and space logistics. Very early.

companies.name: Blue Origin
companies.why: Big, well-funded rocket company in Kent. Its own careers site has no feed, so check it by hand.

companies.name: Microsoft
companies.why: Runs Azure, the cloud much of the AI boom is built on. Home turf.

companies.name: NVIDIA
companies.why: Makes the chips nearly every AI company runs on. The purest picks-and-shovels company there is.

companies.name: Google
companies.why: Google Cloud and its own AI chips (TPUs). Large offices in Seattle and Kirkland.

companies.name: Meta
companies.why: Builds some of the largest AI data centers and infrastructure. Big Bellevue and Seattle presence.

companies.name: Databricks
companies.why: The data and AI platform big companies run on. Still private, so equity is still on the table. Has a Seattle office.
